verses.1: And Queen Sheba heard the name of Solomon, and she came to visit him in his palace.
verses.2: And Jerusalem was entered into by a very noble army. They carried on their shoulders garments, gold, and precious stones. Then they went to Solomon and told him everything that had happened in their hearts.
verses.3: And Solomon told her all her requests. Not a single thing was left unknown to the king, who did not tell her about them.
verses.4: And Queen Sheba saw all of Solomon’s wisdom and the house he built.
verses.5: And he eats what we send him, and he sustains his servants. He also performs the duties of his offices. He feeds them and takes care of them. And he ascends to the house of Jehovah, where there is no more room for any other soul.
verses.6: And he said to the king, “It is true that I have heard about your words and your wisdom in my own land.”
verses.7: And I did not believe those words until I arrived there. My eyes saw for themselves, and it became clear to me that the half who was wise and good was not what I had heard about.
verses.8: You, your people, your servants—these who stand before you, they always hear your wisdom.
verses.9: May Jehovah your God be blessed, who desires to give you the throne over Israel, with love for Jehovah, forever. And may He make you king, so that you may practice justice and righteousness.
verses.10: And she gave the king one hundred and twenty pieces of gold, along with countless pieces of precious stone. There wasn’t enough gold or precious stones to fill those containers. Most of these treasures were given by the Queen of Sheba to King Solomon.
verses.11: And I, too, am a chosen one; I have carried gold from Ophir. I brought back from Ophir countless trees of almug, as well as precious stones.
verses.12: And the king made of cedar trees doors for the House of Jehovah, as well as doors for the palace and the royal chambers. But those doors were not made from cedar wood; they still haven’t been built yet.
verses.13: And King Solomon gave to Queen Sheba all the things she asked for. These were given to her by King Solomon’s hand. Then she went back to her own land, and served her king there.
verses.14: And the weight of the gold that came to Shlomo in one year was equal to sixty shekels, or sixty shekels each.
verses.15: Only those who are not involved in trade or commerce, and all the kings of the land, as well as all the goods of the earth.
verses.16: King Solomon ordered that six gold crowns be made. These crowns were then placed on each of the two crowns.
verses.17: And three ounces of gold were used to cover that shield. Three ounces of gold were also used to cover the other shield. The king gave them to Beit Yaar HaLvanon.
verses.18: And the king made a large throne, and it was covered with gold.
verses.19: Six peaks rise towards the sky; a wheel’s hub also rises towards the sky from behind it. Hands are placed at these points, and two arrows stand beside those hands.
verses.20: And twelve lions stood there on those six hills. But this never happened to any other kings.
verses.21: And all the vessels used by King Solomon were made of gold. All the utensils in the Temple of God were also made of gold. There was no silver at all during the time of Solomon’s reign.
verses.22: For I will inherit the kingdom of kings over the seas. With my brother Hiram, I will reign for three years. I will inherit gold and silver, precious stones, and other valuables.
verses.23: King Solomon was the most wise and intelligent king of all the kings of the earth.
verses.24: And all the earth seeks to hear Shlomo’s wisdom, which God has placed in his heart.
verses.25: And they bring with them from their homes all kinds of gold and silver objects, as well as pearls, jewels, and other valuable items. They also bring along horses and other livestock for use during the year.
verses.26: Shlomo gathered his chariots and soldiers. He had eight thousand chariots and twelve thousand soldiers. He settled in the cities of the chariots, along with the king in Jerusalem.
verses.27: And the king gave the money in Jerusalem as gifts. The pebbles, on the other hand, were given as offerings, and those that were in pieces were also given as offerings.
verses.28: And from those horses that Shlomo brought from Egypt, and from the treasures of the king’s treasury, they would take some of them.
verses.29: And she got off the chariot from Egypt, with six talents of silver and fifty horses. And so, they went away with all these treasures in their hands, for the kings of Hittite and the kings of Assyria.
